chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to him: You are My guest and you are visiting Me; upon Me is your reward, and I have obligated Paradise for you due to your love for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical weight of ziyarat al-akh, framing social bonds as direct conduits to divine proximity. It underscores the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity, where the act of visiting is not merely social but a spiritual transaction that guarantees Paradise through the sincerity of one's love for the believer.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who visits his brother in his house, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says to him: “You are My<sup>azwj</sup> guest and visiting Me<sup>azwj</sup>, upon Me<sup>azwj</sup> is your Reward, and I<sup>azwj</sup> Obligate the Paradise for you due to your love for him”’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘If one visits his brother (in belief) in his house, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will say, ‘You are My guest and My visitor, your service is on Me and I, for your loving him, have made paradise obligatory for you.”’
